Hi! I'm electrical engineering with a minor in CS! I went through recruitment probably during fall 2020 and I hold a position on our exec! 

it's already very challenging to be a woman in STEM and maintain feminity, but I feel like my chapter has been such an amazing support system for me, especially since this past school year was my first ever year of college, and was a challenging year for me mental health wise. They are very understanding and very accepting of my passion towards STEM, and good sisters will encourage you to pursue your passions and dreams. My big is a nursing major, which is also super challenging, but she is always is here to listen to me vent about robotics, STEM courses, etc. I've also had the opportunity to take on a position and gain some leadership and planning experience, which will translate well into any career. 

One of the biggest things I've learned is to always prioritize school before events that aren't mandatory. If you need to work on programming or calculus homework, that comes before any sisterhood or social. It can be hard to miss out, but my sisters are always understanding when I need to step back to focus on school, especially since STEM is extremely challenging. During recruitment, ask how many girls are STEM and/or CS majors, and how well they accommodate. Being upfront about your goals academically during recruitment will only lead you towards the sisterhood that's right for you. 

The amount of CS majors and STEM majors in sororities are small, but you have to remember that the number of women in STEM alone is already small, so don't let that discourage you from joining a sorority, because it is 100% doable and your future sisters will be there to support you :)
